agnostic_oa_boundary_reduction_birth_dea.boundary_or_failure: Correct decoding depends on a total simplex order in which faces precede cofaces and earlier filtration simplices precede genuinely later ones, together with homology over a field and the stated column-reduction convention. Different tie orders may change representative columns while leaving the persistence intervals invariant. A malformed order, coefficient ring, or pivot definition invalidates the pairing semantics, and the standard algorithm has cubic worst-case complexity in the number of simplices.
agnostic_oa_boundary_reduction_birth_dea.interpretation: The source changes representation from a filtered complex to one boundary matrix. Rows and columns follow a filtration-compatible simplex order, so the matrix simultaneously records face relations and time of entry. Left-to-right column additions make the lowest nonzero row index unique among nonzero columns. A final pivot low(j)=i pairs the simplex entering at i, which births a feature, with the simplex entering at j, which kills it; a birth column never used as a later pivot yields an infinite interval. Algebraic elimination thus exposes the interval endpoints implicit in the filtered inclusions.
agnostic_oa_boundary_reduction_birth_dea.nonparaphrase_operation: Linearize a filtered incidence structure with an order respecting both dependency and filtration, build its boundary operator over the chosen field, and reduce columns until pivot indices are unique. Decode each pivot pair through the filtration grades, and distinguish zero columns later paired from zero columns that remain unpaired. Validate that decoded intervals are invariant under allowable tie reorderings even if representatives differ.

That easier construction does not remove worst-case combinatorial explosion, so practical computations often truncate dimension or use sparsified alternatives. Approximation guarantee, construction interface, and object size are separate properties that must all be audited.
